title: MADRec: Reliable Multi-Agent Reasoning with Evidence-Grounded Debate for Recommendation
summary: Innovation: To address this issue, we propose Multi-Agent Debate-based Recommendation (MADRec), an evidence-grounded multi-agent framework that enhances the reliability of multi-agent recommendation reasoning. Why it matters: candidate generation sets the recall ceiling for everything downstream in the recommendation pipeline.

title: C3H: Compression-to-Consensus Criteria Hijacking in Multimodal LLM Recommender Systems
summary: Innovation: In this paper, we introduce C3H, a novel inference-time attack that exploits this vulnerability. Why it matters: better ordering of candidates directly lifts clicks, conversions, and user satisfaction.

title: User-Adaptive Fusion of Multiple Foundation Models for Recommender Systems
summary: Innovation: Motivated by this observation, we introduce UF2O, a user-adaptive approach for fusing multiple foundation models for recommendation. Why it matters: a shared foundation model could serve ranking, retrieval, and targeting from one backbone.

title: SARA: An Auditor-in-the-Loop LLM Recommender for Sustainability Reports
summary: Innovation: We present SARA (Sustainability Reporting Assistant), a human-in-the-loop recommender system delivered as a Microsoft Word add-in that recommends, for each requirement, the passages addressing it and… Why it matters: shows what LLMs add beyond classic ID-based models in production-style recsys.

title: MoR4Rec: Mixture-of-Recursion for Sequential Recommendation
summary: Innovation: To address this issue, we propose MoR4Rec, a sequential recommendation framework based on a Mixture-of-Recursion paradigm, which enables item-wise adaptive computation through a shared transformer… Why it matters: richer sequence models capture intent as it evolves over time.

title: Beyond Relevance: An Empirical Study of Multimodal LLMs for Diversity-Aware Recommendation Reranking
summary: Innovation: Large language models (LLMs) have emerged as promising rerankers for recommendation, yet most existing approaches rely on textual item descriptions and primarily focus on relevance. Why it matters: richer sequence models capture intent as it evolves over time.

title: Grounding User Preferences in Shared Multimodal Concepts for Recommendation
summary: Innovation: We introduce MKGE, a multimodal knowledge graph framework that represents these factors as canonical, addressable concepts. Why it matters: shows what LLMs add beyond classic ID-based models in production-style recsys.

title: RecField: Embedding Recommendations into Spatial Movie Organization as Affordances for Serendipitous Encounters
summary: Innovation: We propose RecField, a spatial movie organization interface where users freely arrange movies into collection zones. Why it matters: relevant to how candidates are retrieved, ranked, and served to users.

title: Towards Realistic Evaluation of Uncertainty Quantification for LLM-Based Recommender Systems
summary: Innovation: Here we introduce a fixed-ranking benchmark which evaluates eight heterogeneous UQ signals as record-level monitors under a shared output contract. Why it matters: better ordering of candidates directly lifts clicks, conversions, and user satisfaction.

title: Speculative Decoding for Semantic-ID-Based Generative Recommendations
summary: Innovation: We propose SIDECAR, which uses approximate draft candidates and a tree-attention pass to score the entire draft in a single model call, memory permitting. Why it matters: generating candidates directly could reshape the classic retrieve-then-rank pipeline.
